turn_order.title: Turn order and speed
turn_order.summary: Moves execute in priority brackets first, then by speed; equal speed is a 50/50 coin flip. Trick Room inverts the speed comparison.
details: Switches always resolve before moves, in any speed order.
Priority brackets: Protect +4, Fake Out +3, Extreme Speed +2, most status moves 0, Trick Room -7. A higher bracket moves first regardless of speed.
Within a bracket, higher Speed stat moves first; an exact speed tie is decided randomly each turn.
Trick Room (while active, 5 turns) reverses the speed comparison: the SLOWER Pokemon moves first. Speed boosts and penalties still apply before the inversion.
Common speed modifiers: Tailwind doubles your side's Speed, paralysis quarters it, Icy Wind/Electroweb lower by one stage, Choice Scarf multiplies by 1.5x.

spread_moves.title: Spread moves in doubles
spread_moves.summary: Moves that target 'all adjacent foes' hit both opponents at 0.75x power; the discount stays even if one foe faints mid-turn.
details: Spread moves (Rock Slide, Earthquake, Dazzling Gleam, Icy Wind, Eruption...) deal 75% power to EACH of the two foes — usually more total damage than one full-power hit, less per target.
Wide Guard (priority +3) protects a side from spread moves entirely; Feint breaks it.
Accuracy is rolled per target: a 90% Rock Slide can hit one foe and miss the other.
Spread moves ignore redirection (Follow Me/Rage Powder do not pull them).
Single-target moves keep full 100% power — prefer them when you need to KO one specific threat.

protect.title: Protect and detection
protect.summary: Protect blocks most damaging and status moves that turn, but consecutive uses decay to 1/3 then 1/9 success.
details: Priority +4: always resolves before attacks.
Consecutive Protect success: ~100% -> 1/3 -> 1/9...; resetting by choosing another action restores 100%.
Bypassed by Feint, Hyperspace Fury, attacks that ignore protection, and by status moves that set entry hazards or weather.
In doubles Protect is a tempo tool: scout the opponent's choices, stall a Trick Room or weather turn, or shield while a partner sets up.
Fake Out (priority +3, first turn out only) is NOT blocked-piercing but only flinches; it is a common lead option alongside Protect.

redirection.title: Redirection
redirection.summary: Follow Me / Rage Powder pull single-target moves onto the redirector, shielding the partner; some immunities resist the pull.
details: Follow Me and Ally Switch have priority +2; Rage Powder +2 but is a powder move: Grass-types, Overcoat and Safety Goggles ignore it.
Lightning Rod (Electric) and Storm Drain (Water) draw moves of their type, negate the damage, and raise the redirector's Special Attack by one stage.
Redirection only affects single-target moves aimed at that side; spread moves, self-targeting and already-locked targets are unaffected.
Classic use: redirect attacks away from a frail sweeper or a Trick Room setter for one turn.

weather.title: Weather
weather.summary: Rain boosts Water 1.5x and weakens Fire 0.5x; sun does the reverse; sand/snow chip non-immunes and buff defensive types.
details: Rain: Water x1.5, Fire x0.5, Hurricane and Thunder never miss, hydration/dry-skin heal. Sun: Fire x1.5, Water x0.5, Solar Beam no charge.
Sandstorm chips 1/16 per turn (Rock/Ground/Steel immune); Snow chips 1/16 (Ice immune) and boosts Ice mons' Defense 1.5x.
Weather abilities set it on entry (Drizzle/Drought/Sand Stream/Snow Warning) — overriding a previous weather; moves set 5 turns (8 with the rocks).
Ability-weather (Drizzle etc.) is permanent until replaced; the move-based counter cannot override it.
VGC tempo: weather wars decide damage math — check the current weather before picking a STAB move.

terrain.title: Terrain
terrain.summary: Terrains only affect grounded Pokemon: Electric prevents sleep, Grassy heals 1/16 and weakens Earthquake, Misty blocks status, Psychic blocks priority.
details: Electric Terrain: grounded mons cannot be put to sleep and Electric moves gain 1.3x power.
Grassy Terrain: heals grounded mons 1/16 each turn, boosts Grass 1.3x, weakens Earthquake/Magnitude/Bulldoze 0.5x.
Misty Terrain: grounded mons are immune to non-volatile status and confusion, Dragon moves halved against them.
Psychic Terrain: grounded mons cannot be hit by priority moves (blocks Fake Out and Extreme Speed), Psychic 1.3x.
Terrains last 5 turns (8 with extenders), replace each other, and coexist with weather — both can be active at once.

status.title: Status conditions
status.summary: Burn halves physical damage and chips; Toxic poison escalates; paralysis quarters speed and 25% full-stops; sleep/freeze disable.
details: Burn: 1/16 chip per turn, physical damage halved (Fire-types immune).
Poison: 1/8 chip (Steel/Poison immune); Toxic poison adds another 1/16 per turn stayed. Toxic counts RESET on switch.
Paralysis: Speed x0.25, 25% chance to be fully paralyzed. No type is immune in Gen 9 (Limber prevents it on the holder).
Sleep: 1-3 turns in Gen 9, waking removes the status; blocked by Electric Terrain. Misty Terrain blocks ALL non-volatile status on grounded mons.
Sleep Clause is NOT standard in VGC: you may put several opposing Pokemon to sleep.
Freeze: thaw 20% per turn, Fire moves and Scald thaw the user; a frozen mon is effectively removed from the game until then.

stat_stages.title: Stat stages
stat_stages.summary: Each stage multiplies the stat: +1 = 1.5x, +2 = 2x, +3 = 2.5x; negatives mirror (-1 = 2/3, -2 = 0.5x), clamped at +/-6.
details: Stage multipliers: 2/8, 2/7, 2/6 (0.67), 2/5 (0.5), 2/4 (0.4), 2/3 (0.29) for -6..-1; +1 1.5x, +2 2x, +3 2.5x, +4 3x, +5 3.5x, +6 4x. Accuracy/evasion use a different table.
Critical hits ignore the ATTACKER's negative stages and the DEFENDER's positive defense stages.
Common VGC stat movers: Intimidate (-1 Atk on entry, both foes in doubles), Snarl/Icy Wind (-1 Atk/SpA or Spe to both foes), Parting Shot, Swords Dance/Nasty Plot (+2).
Contrary inverts changes; Simple doubles them; stat changes are cleared on switching out.
Spread stat-drops (Snarl, Icy Wind, Struggle Bug) hit BOTH foes — often better tempo than raw damage.

tera.title: Terastallization
tera.summary: Once per battle, one of your Pokemon terastallizes: its defensive type becomes the Tera type while keeping STAB bonuses.
details: Once per battle each side may terastallize exactly one Pokemon, one time.
Defensively the mon becomes a mono-type of its Tera type (loses all other defensive types); abilities, items and status persist.
Offensively it keeps STAB on its ORIGINAL types AND gains STAB on the Tera type; a Tera type matching an original type doubles that STAB to 2x instead of 1.5x.
Terastallizing also removes some type-based effects? No — it keeps abilities and items; status persists.
Tera is a one-shot defensive or offensive flip: identify the opponent's likely Tera type (from team context) before committing to a KO move.
Tera Stellar: 1.5x per move type used once per type, no defensive change.

doubles_specific.title: Doubles-only mechanics
doubles_specific.summary: Doubles adds spread moves, per-slot targeting, support moves (Wide Guard, Helping Hand, Feint), and speed-tie chaos.
details: You pick two actions per turn, one per slot — they resolve in speed order, and a mon KOed before acting never moves (protect or faster KO matters).
Wide Guard (+3): protects the whole side from spread moves. Quick Guard: blocks priority. Feint (+2): breaks protection and these guards.
Helping Hand (+5): partner's move gains 1.5x — the strongest single-turn damage boost.
A target that faints before a single-target move resolves makes the move fail — overkill into an already-dying slot wastes the hit.
Two foes at equal speed to you: you can still be outsped by either via the random tie.
Level 50 flat rules: damage variance is +/-15%; EVs are halved in effect (4 EVs = 1 stat point at 50).

weather.RAINDANCE: RAIN is up: Water moves x1.5, Fire x0.5, Hurricane/Thunder always hit.
weather.SUNNYDAY: SUN is up: Fire moves x1.5, Water x0.5, Solar Beam needs no charge.
weather.SANDSTORM: SAND is up: 1/16 chip per turn to non-Rock/Ground/Steel mons.
weather.SNOWSCAPE: SNOW is up: 1/16 chip per turn, Ice-type Defense boosted 1.5x.
weather.HAIL: HAIL is up: 1/16 chip per turn to non-Ice mons.
weather.DESOLATELAND: Harsh sun (Desolate Land): Water moves fail entirely.
weather.PRIMORDIALSEA: Heavy rain (Primordial Sea): Fire moves fail entirely.
weather.DELTASTREAM: Strong winds (Delta Stream): supereffective Flying damage is neutralized.

fields.TRICK_ROOM: TRICK ROOM is active: the SLOWER Pokemon moves first — reconsider your speed assumptions.
fields.ELECTRIC_TERRAIN: Electric Terrain: grounded mons can't fall asleep; Electric damage x1.3.
fields.GRASSY_TERRAIN: Grassy Terrain: grounded mons heal 1/16 per turn; Earthquake damage halved.
fields.MISTY_TERRAIN: Misty Terrain: grounded mons can't be statused or confused.
fields.PSYCHIC_TERRAIN: Psychic Terrain: priority moves don't hit grounded mons; Psychic damage x1.3.
fields.GRAVITY: Gravity is active: accuracy +5/6 and Flying mons can be hit by Ground moves.
fields.NEUTRALIZING_GAS: Neutralizing Gas: all abilities are suppressed while this Pokemon is on the field.
fields.MAGIC_ROOM: Magic Room: held items have no effect.
fields.WONDER_ROOM: Wonder Room: Defense and Sp. Def stats are swapped.
fields.MUD_SPOT: Mud Sport: Electric damage on this field is reduced (x0.33).
fields.WATER_SPORT: Water Sport: Fire damage on this field is reduced (x0.33).
fields.FAIRY_LOCK: Fairy Lock: grounded mons cannot switch out next turn.
fields.HEAL_BLOCK: Heal Block: healing moves and effects fail.
